the leakage current increase in heavily C-doped GaAs is induced by two types of defects, i.e., defects formed by C-H complex decomposition and those formed by REDR.
the degradation in the C-doping GaAs-based devices induced under minority-carrier-injection conditions is due to the C-related defects.

the degradation of GaAs HBTs.
the degradation of GaAs/AlAs hetero-juction bipolar transistors with C-doped base.
the degradation of GaAs HBTs under minority-carrier injections.

H-related defects and the defects formed by thermal annealing are the causes of degradation under minority-carrier injections.
the H-related defects induce the degradation under minority-carrier injections, and the C-related defects induce the device degradation.

C-H complexes are the main cause of degradation under minority-carrier injections and that the defects induced by high-temperature processing are also responsible.
